Risk Title: Privileged cloud or identity admin account misused or compromised
Risk Description: An attacker phishes or steals the session of a user holding production AdministratorAccess, Okta Super Admin, or GitHub owner, then exfiltrates PHI or destroys infrastructure.
Asset / Process: AWS wcp-prod admin plane, Okta tenant, GitHub org
Threat: External actor (phishing, session-token theft) or malicious/negligent insider
Vulnerability: Excess admin grants; admin performed from daily-use accounts; no JIT elevation
Existing Controls: Okta SSO+MFA for most users; CloudTrail and GuardDuty; MDR 24x7; Vault Lock on backups
Planned Mitigation: Remove excess grants; -adm accounts; JIT elevation; GitHub owner cap (POAM-003)
Rationale: Inherent: L4: identity-based intrusion is the dominant cloud attack path. I5: admin reaches all PHI (>50k records) and can cause an outage over 24h.
Rationale: Current: L3: MFA and monitoring raise attacker effort, but 6 unjustified or daily-account admin assignments existed. I5 unchanged: any admin can still reach everything.
Rationale: Residual: L2: -adm accounts with phishing-resistant MFA plus approval-gated JIT elevation. I4: time-boxed sessions and Vault Lock limit destructive impact and dwell time, but exfiltration during a session is still possible.

Risk Title: Unauthorized access by former employees or contractors
Risk Description: A departed worker's still-active account is used, by them or by an attacker, to access PHI or financial systems.
Asset / Process: All in-scope systems, including Ledgerline and the vendor portal
Threat: Former workforce member (disgruntled or careless), or an attacker using an orphaned account
Vulnerability: Manual de-provisioning; local accounts outside SSO; contractor end dates not enforced
Existing Controls: Okta deactivation by IT ticket; asset recovery at exit
Planned Mitigation: HR-to-Okta reconciliation with auto-ticketing; contractor expiry; local-account cleanup (POAM-001, POAM-006)
Rationale: Inherent: L4: turnover of about 38/year plus contractors, and orphaned accounts are a well-known misuse path. I4: AWS admin or PHI DB access affects 500–50,000+ records; limited by role mix.
Rationale: Current: L4 unchanged: the control failed testing (2 of 19 not disabled, 1 post-termination sign-in, local admin account active 95 days) and earns no credit. I4.
Rationale: Residual: L2: daily reconciliation job, contractor account expiry, and a local-account inventory, validated 7 of 7. I4 unchanged: a missed account could still reach sensitive data.

Risk Description: An attacker obtains the password of an MFA-exempt account and signs in directly, inheriting that user's access, including identity administration.
Threat: Credential phishing, password spraying, reuse of breached credentials
Vulnerability: MFA exemption group (9 humans incl. an Okta Super Admin); IAM user without MFA
Existing Controls: Global MFA policy for 97% of users; replay-resistant authenticators; Okta ThreatInsight
Planned Mitigation: Delete the exemption policy; enroll all users; phishing-resistant admin MFA; exception workflow (POAM-002)
Rationale: Inherent: L4: phishing is the leading initial-access vector. I5: federation reaches AWS prod and PHI.
Rationale: Current: L3: MFA covers 97%, a partial control. I5: an exempt Okta Super Admin could reach everything.
Rationale: Residual: L2: no exemptions; phishing-resistant MFA for admins; token theft still possible. I4: least-privilege work narrows what one account reaches.

Risk Description: Users accumulate access beyond need over time, increasing the blast radius of any compromise or misuse.
Asset / Process: Privileged and PHI entitlements across 9 systems
Threat: Insider misuse; attacker leveraging over-privileged accounts
Vulnerability: Rubber-stamp reviews; privileged systems out of review scope; no re-baseline on transfer
Rationale: Inherent: L4: fast growth, transfers, and contractors make creep near-certain without review. I3: creep usually adds read access; worst credible case is fewer than 500 records.
Rationale: Current: L4: the review operated but was ineffective (100% approval, key systems excluded), so no credit. I3.
Rationale: Residual: L2: full-scope campaigns with usage data and flagged items needing rationale. I3.

Risk Title: Inability to detect or investigate PHI access
Risk Description: Misuse goes unnoticed, or a breach found months later cannot be scoped, forcing presumptive notification of large patient populations.
Asset / Process: Audit logs (CloudTrail, application PHI-access audit, SIEM)
Threat: Undetected insider or attacker activity; late-discovered breach
Existing Controls: Comprehensive event logging (AU-2); immutable log archive (AU-9); MDR alerting (SI-4)
Planned Mitigation: Extend retention (POAM-008, done); backup reviewer and escalation (POAM-009)
Rationale: Inherent: L3: breaches are often discovered after 90+ days. I4: inability to scope means broad notification plus contract breach.
Rationale: Current: L3: logging is strong, but retention is short and 35% of weekly reviews were missed or incomplete. I4.
Rationale: Residual: L2: 400-day retention plus a backup reviewer. I3: records now exist to scope and limit notification.

Risk Description: An attacker exploits a known, unpatched flaw in a production service or host to gain a foothold.
Threat: Opportunistic exploitation of known CVEs; ransomware affiliates
Vulnerability: 23% SLA misses; end-of-life runtimes; exception process unused
Existing Controls: WAF; weekly authenticated scanning; container image scanning; EDR; MDR
Planned Mitigation: Upgrade EOL runtimes; exception process; SLA reporting; tag enforcement (POAM-010)
Rationale: Inherent: L4: exploitation of known vulnerabilities is a top initial-access vector. I5: PHI platform compromise.
Rationale: Current: L3: scanning, WAF, and EDR are effective layers, but 6 items are open past SLA. I4: segmentation (private subnets) limits the blast radius from most workloads.
Rationale: Residual: L2: SLA adherence with governed exceptions. I4: same architecture.

Risk Title: Compromise of unsupported legacy components in the PHI path
Risk Description: An attacker exploits an unpatchable flaw on the legacy SFTP host, which holds the nightly full-PHI extract, and pivots or exfiltrates.
Vulnerability: No vendor patches; host previously exposed via internet-facing RDP
Existing Controls: EDR; SFTP source allowlist; weekly scanning; SSM-only admin (after FIND-012 fix)
Planned Mitigation: Decommission wf-sftp-01 and legacy-reports; upgrade notify-worker (POAM-011)
Rationale: Inherent: L4: unsupported, internet-reachable Windows host. I4: a full-PHI extract sits there transiently (worst credible case is one night's file, bounded).
Rationale: Current: L3: RDP closed, allowlist and EDR in place, but no patches. I4.
Rationale: Residual: L1: components decommissioned (Avoid). I4 kept, because the managed-transfer replacement still moves the same data.

Risk Title: Failed or slow recovery from ransomware or data corruption
Risk Description: A destructive event forces recovery, and recovery takes longer than RTO or loses data because the process was never exercised.
Vulnerability: Restore never tested (at fieldwork); contingency plan untested
Existing Controls: PITR (35 days); cross-region, cross-account backups with Vault Lock; BC/DR plan
Planned Mitigation: Semi-annual restore tests (POAM-013, done); CP exercise (POAM-014)
Rationale: Inherent: L3: healthcare ransomware frequency. I5: outage over 24h for clinical workflows.
Rationale: Current: L2: strong, immutable backups reduce the chance of an unrecoverable event. I5: recovery time was unproven.
Rationale: Residual: L2. I4: restore proven at 3h41m (within the 4h RTO); a full contingency exercise is pending (POAM-014).

Risk Title: Delayed or ineffective response to a major incident
Risk Description: During a major incident, unclear roles or notification steps delay containment or cause a missed contractual or regulatory notification deadline.
Asset / Process: Incident response capability and notification obligations
Threat: Major incident (ransomware, large PHI breach) stressing untested processes
Vulnerability: No IR exercise in 21 months; SHCA 24h path never rehearsed
Existing Controls: IRP-005 (current); 24x7 MDR; incidents in H1 handled well (IR-4 satisfied)
Rationale: Inherent: L3: at least one significant incident per year is plausible. I4: missed notification means a contract breach and regulatory scrutiny.
Rationale: Current: L3: good day-to-day handling, but major-incident paths are untested. I4.
Rationale: Residual: L2: rehearsed plan with the SHCA step. I3: faster, coordinated response limits impact.

Risk Title: PHI exposure through the analytics vendor (Quarrystone)
Risk Description: A breach at Quarrystone or its offshore subcontractor exposes Wrenfield PHI, and notice arrives too late for Wrenfield to meet 24h or 5-day obligations.
Asset / Process: Nightly full-PHI extract (about 410k patients) processed by Quarrystone and its subcontractors
Threat: Vendor or subcontractor breach; unauthorized offshore access; delayed breach notice
Vulnerability: Offshore subcontractor access; 30-day notice term; excess data fields; stale pentest
Existing Controls: BAA; SOC 2 Type II (unqualified); encryption in transit and at rest; interim suspension of offshore access (2026-07-24)
Planned Mitigation: Contract amendment; data minimization; pentest and retest; monitoring plan (POAM-016). Transfer (partial) through cyber insurance and vendor indemnity.
Rationale: Inherent: L4: third-party breaches are frequent in healthcare, and an undisclosed offshore party was present. I5: >50k records plus SHCA contract loss.
Rationale: Current: L3: vendor controls are generally mature (SOC 2, encryption) and offshore access is suspended, but the contract terms are unchanged. I5.
Rationale: Residual: L2: contractual US-only with technical enforcement, 24h notice, and current pentest. I4: minimized extract (no contact details or free text) reduces the records and sensitivity exposed.

Risk Description: A compromised dependency or vendor integration introduces malicious code or access into WCP.
Asset / Process: CI/CD pipeline, open-source dependencies, vendor integrations
Threat: Malicious dependency or compromised vendor update or integration
Vulnerability: No C-SCRM plan; no fourth-party inventory; 5 vendors overdue for review
Existing Controls: Dependency scanning; branch protection and required review; OIDC deploy (no static keys); pinned base images
Planned Mitigation: C-SCRM plan; clear the vendor backlog; fourth-party inventory (POAM-015)
Rationale: Inherent: L3: supply-chain attacks are increasing. I5: code execution in the PHI platform.
Rationale: Current: L3: good pipeline hygiene, but no program-level supply chain risk management. I4: OIDC and least-privilege deploy roles limit what a compromised pipeline can reach.
Rationale: Residual: L2: C-SCRM plan, current vendor reviews, fourth-party visibility. I4.

Risk Title: Cloud misconfiguration exposing PHI or admin services
Risk Description: A manual misconfiguration (an open port, a public resource) exposes PHI or an admin interface to the internet.
Asset / Process: AWS wcp-prod network and storage configuration
Threat: Opportunistic internet scanning; misconfiguration exploited by attackers
Vulnerability: Console changes bypass IaC; CSPM findings not routed to on-call
Existing Controls: Org-wide S3 Block Public Access (SCP); encryption by default; Security Hub CIS checks; IaC for most resources
Planned Mitigation: Route CSPM to on-call; admin-port guardrail; emergency change auto-revert (POAM-012, POAM-018)
Rationale: Inherent: L4: misconfiguration is a leading cloud breach cause. I5: public PHI exposure.
Rationale: Current: L2: strong preventive guardrails for data stores (block public access, encryption). The observed exposure was an admin port, not data. I5: remains the worst credible case.
Rationale: Residual: L2: CSPM routed to on-call plus SCP guardrails on admin ports. I4: guardrails prevent the most severe (data-store) exposures.

Risk Title: Fraudulent vendor payment through an SoD conflict
Risk Description: A user alters vendor bank details and approves payments to an attacker-controlled account.
Threat: Insider fraud or coerced insider (business email compromise)
Vulnerability: One user holds vendor-master maintenance and payment approval (≤ $25k)
Existing Controls: Compensating: monthly vendor-master change report reviewed by the Controller; callback verification of bank-detail changes; payments over $25k need CFO approval
Planned Mitigation: RACC-001 risk acceptance with compensating control; split roles at AP backfill (POAM-007)
Rationale: Inherent: L3: BEC-driven bank-change fraud is common. I3: bounded by the $25k approval limit and monthly detection (worst credible case $100k–500k over a month).
Rationale: Current: L2: the compensating review operated 6 of 6 months, plus callbacks. I3.
Rationale: Residual: L2. I3: accepted with the compensating control until the roles are split.

Risk Title: Unauthorized or untested changes cause an outage or security regression
Risk Description: An emergency or console change is made without review and introduces an outage or exposure (FIND-012 is a realized example).
Threat: Human error under time pressure; unreviewed emergency changes
Vulnerability: Emergency and console change paths lack enforced approval and revert
Existing Controls: PR review and CI for code and IaC; protected deploy environments
Rationale: Inherent: L3: frequent changes. I4: multi-hour outage or exposure.
Rationale: Current: L2: 22 of 25 sampled changes were compliant; the pipeline is strong. I4: realized once (FIND-012).
Rationale: Residual: L2. I3: console-change alerting and auto-revert shorten the exposure window.

Risk Title: Phishing and social engineering of the workforce
Risk Description: A user is tricked into disclosing credentials, approving a push, or sending PHI or payments to an attacker.
Existing Controls: MFA with number challenge; email security; phishing simulations (4.3% click rate); help-desk identity verification; EDR
Planned Mitigation: Training enforcement (POAM-019); continue simulations and phishing-resistant MFA rollout
Rationale: Inherent: L5: phishing attempts are constant. I4: credential compromise leading to PHI access.
Rationale: Current: L3: layered controls (MFA, filtering, EDR) catch most attempts (INC-2026-0012 shows MFA blocked a successful phish). I3: least privilege and monitoring limit impact.
Rationale: Residual: L3 and I3 unchanged: training completion is a hygiene fix and does not move the risk. Accepted as within tolerance (Moderate) with an ongoing awareness program.

Risk Title: Loss of SHCA contract or customer trust from unresolved compliance gaps
Risk Description: SHCA or Lakemont judges Wrenfield's remediation insufficient, delaying go-live or leading to termination or non-renewal.
Asset / Process: SHCA C3P contract ($23.4M) and top customer relationships (Lakemont)
Threat: Contract cure notice or termination; customer non-renewal after security review
Vulnerability: Outdated SSP; open High POA&M items near go-live; vendor conditions unmet
Existing Controls: This assessment and the POA&M; executive sponsorship; customer communication plan
Planned Mitigation: Close High POA&M items before go-live; SSP rewrite (POAM-017); proactive customer update
Rationale: Inherent: L3: 7 High findings against a 90-day rule. I5: loss of a $23.4M contract or a customer worth 21% of ARR.
Rationale: Current: L3: strong remediation momentum (7 of 19 closed in 6 weeks), but 3 High items are open with dependencies. I4: SHCA would more likely require a cure plan than terminate.
Rationale: Residual: L2: High items closed before 2027-01-11, and the SSP is accurate. I3.

Risk Description: A stolen long-lived service credential grants quiet, unmonitored access to PHI extracts.
Asset / Process: Non-human accounts with static credentials (SFTP push, reporting ETL, vendor logins)
Threat: Credential theft from hosts or repositories; vendor-side compromise
Vulnerability: Keys 1.5–3 years old; no owners; a shared vendor login
Existing Controls: Secrets Manager rotation for DB credentials; OIDC for CI/CD
Planned Mitigation: Owners, rotation or federation, and named vendor accounts (POAM-005)
Rationale: Inherent: L3: static keys leak through repositories, hosts, and backups. I4: PHI extract access.
Rationale: Current: L3: modern patterns exist, but the legacy exceptions carry the risk. I4.
Rationale: Residual: L1: federation and rotation with owners and quarterly attestation. I4: a compromised service identity would still reach the same data.

Risk Title: Loss or theft of an endpoint containing PHI
Risk Description: A lost or stolen laptop exposes PHI stored locally.
Existing Controls: Full-disk encryption (100%); MDM remote wipe; policy against storing PHI locally, with DLP; EDR
Planned Mitigation: None beyond current controls; annual review
Rationale: Inherent: L4: several devices are lost each year. I3: a local PHI cache could hold under 500 records.
Rationale: Current: L2: devices are still lost (INC-2026-0063), but FDE means a lost encrypted device is not a breach of unsecured PHI. I2: exposure is internal-only and non-reportable when encryption is verified.
